fluff.overview: The Xiphos, named for an ancient Greek double-edged sword, was developed by Irian Technologies for the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth. Entering service in 3116, the assault-class battle armor was designed to protect infantry against artillery bombardment, one of the most effective countermeasures against powered armor formations. Weighing two thousand kilograms, the Xiphos carries specialized protective plating and an advanced communications suite resistant to electronic countermeasures. Three standard weapon configurations offer flexibility ranging from ballistic firepower to thermal detection and area denial. The suit earned a strong reputation for durability and reliable performance across both defensive and offensive operations.
fluff.capabilities:
The Xiphos mounts close to a full ton of reactive armor, providing assault-class protection with particular resistance to explosive munitions and indirect fire. A basic manipulator on the right arm allows limited object handling, while modular weapon mounts on both arms give the suit configuration flexibility. An improved communications system allows battlefield coordination even under active electronic countermeasures.

Configuration B replaces the ballistic weapons with a plasma rifle and a one-shot short-range missile launcher. The plasma rifle generates extreme heat on impact, forcing BattleMech pilots to manage rising thermal loads while dealing significant damage to conventional infantry and light armor. The single SRM round provides an opening salvo, allowing troopers to soften targets before closing to plasma range. This loadout makes the B configuration particularly dangerous to units that rely on heat management for combat effectiveness. The plasma rifle’s twenty-round ammunition supply provides enough endurance for sustained engagements, and the combination of heat-inducing weapons with the suit’s heavy armor makes this configuration effective in close-quarters combat.
fluff.deployment: Clan Wolf Points fielding the B configuration used the plasma weaponry in close-quarters engagements where its heat-generating effects could be exploited against Inner Sphere opponents. Wolf warriors, accustomed to heat-intensive combat in OmniMechs, adapted quickly to directing plasma fire against enemy armor and fortifications during conquest operations across the former Free Worlds League.
fluff.history:
The Xiphos grew out of Irian Technologies’ efforts to address artillery bombardment, one of powered infantry’s oldest and deadliest vulnerabilities. Commissioned by the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth, the suit entered production in 3116 at facilities on both Irian and Washburn. Its reactive armor gave troopers meaningful protection against indirect fire for the first time, filling a long-standing capability gap in battle armor design.

Commonwealth forces put the Xiphos to effective use across numerous engagements during the Dark Age. Militia units on Laureles proved the suit’s communications resilience under electronic warfare conditions in 3118. The Eighth Free Worlds Legionnaires employed Xiphos troopers in a covert 3125 raid on Corey, dropping them directly into Hollis Incorporated’s facilities to seize Catapult spare parts. During the Wolf Empire’s invasion of the former Free Worlds League, Commonwealth defenders repeatedly ambushed Wolf artillery positions using helicopter-delivered Xiphos formations on Autumn Wind and several other contested worlds. The tactic proved effective until the battle for Washburn, where prepared Wolf forces overwhelmed the defenders with battle armored troops positioned behind their own artillery. Washburn’s fall brought one production line under Clan Wolf control, and Wolf warriors quickly adopted the suit for their own formations.
